topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: The room feels colder, the air thinner, as I learn the pieces of my past aren’t as solid as I thought. It’s as if someone has taken a fine brush and carefully painted over the edges of my history, making the lines blurry, indistinct. The memories we shared, the secrets we kept, the laughter—the lightness of those days feels heavy now, like it’s sinking into the ground. I keep reaching out, hoping for a familiar hand to grasp mine, but the space between us has grown too wide. I’m not sure I can call out loud enough for you to hear, or if there’s even anyone there to listen anymore.
